extracted.intended_audience: industrial property owners, applicants, representatives, attorneys, and state authorities operating under Vietnam industrial property law
extracted.subtask_description: Statutory standards and procedural requirements governing industrial property in Vietnam, including unfair competition, provisional rights, limitations, assignment and licensing rules, compulsory licensing, representation, and plant variety protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts of unfair competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The following acts shall be acts of unfair competition: a) Using commercial indications that cause confusion as to business entities or business activities or commercial source of goods or services; b) Using commercial indications that cause confusion as to the origin, production method, feature, quality, quantity or other characteristics of goods or services; or as to the conditions for provision of goods and services; c) Using a mark being protected in a country which is party to an international treaty to which the Socialist Republic of Vietnam is a party ... if the user was a representative or agent of the mark owner and such use was neither consented to by the mark owner nor justified; d) Registering or possessing the right to use or using a domain name identical with or confusingly similar to a protected trade name or mark of another person, or a geographical indication that one does not have the right to use, for the purpose of possessing the domain name, benefiting from or prejudicing reputation and goodwill of the respective mark, trade name and geographical indication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 3 clarifies use includes affixing on goods/packaging, selling, advertising, storing for sale and importing goods affixed with such commercial indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of commercial indications
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial indications mean signs, information serving as guidelines to trade of goods and services, including marks, trade names, business symbols, business slogans, geographical indications, package designs, label designs, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of such commercial indications includes affixing on goods, packaging, service means, transaction documents and advertising; selling, advertising, storing for sale and importing goods affixed with such indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights to inventions, industrial designs and layout designs (notice right)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an applicant for registration of an invention or industrial design knows that the invention or industrial design is being used by another person for commercial purposes without prior use right, the applicant shall have the right to serve a written notice of his or her application filing specifying the filing date and date of publication to such user so that the latter shall terminate or continue such use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies also to layout-designs of semiconductor integrated circuits that were commercially exploited by the person having the right to registration or licensee prior to grant (Article 131.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to request remuneration after grant for continued use
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notified person keeps using such invention, industrial design or layout design and a Protection Title (Invention Patent, Utility solution Patent, Industrial Design Patent or Layout-design registration Certificate) is issued, the owner shall have the right to request such user to pay a remuneration equivalent to the fee for licensing such invention, industrial design or layout design within the relevant scope and period of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remuneration is tied to licensing fees for the relevant scope/period of use (Article 131.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors limiting industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Under this Law, industrial property rights may be limited by: 1. Rights of prior users to the invention or industrial design; 2. Obligations of the owners including: a) To pay remuneration to the authors of inventions, industrial designs or layout designs; b) To use the inventions or marks; and 3. To transfer the right to use inventions under decisions of State authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are statutory limitations that can permit others to use or constrain owners' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: State right to use inventions (use on behalf of the State)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ministries and ministerial-level authorities shall have the right to, on behalf of the State, use or allow others to use inventions in their fields for public non-commercial purposes, national defense, security, disease prevention, treatment and nutrition and other urgent social needs without obtaining permission of the invention owner or licensee, in accordance with Articles 145 and 146.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use under paragraph 1 is limited to scope and conditions of licensing provided in Article 146.1, except for inventions created using State funds (Article 133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior use right to inventions and industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who, before the publication date of a registration application, used or made necessary preparation for use of an invention or industrial design identical to the protected one, but created independently (prior use right holder), shall be entitled after Protection Title grant to continue such use within the same scope and volume of use or preparation made before the publication date without permission or compensation to the owner; such use is not an infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior use right is non-transferable except when transferred together with the business or production premises where the use/preparation was made; the holder cannot expand scope/volume unless permitted by the owner (Article 134).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to pay remuneration to authors of inventions, industrial designs and layout designs
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner shall have the obligation to pay remuneration to the author except where otherwise agreed. Minimum remuneration rates: a) 10% of the revenue gained by the owner from the use of the invention/industrial design/layout design; b) 15% of the total amount of money received by the owner on each payment upon the granting of a license of the invention/industrial design/layout design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where multiple authors exist, the rate applies to all authors together and they allocate among themselves; the obligation lasts for the whole term of protection (Article 135).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to use inventions and marks
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of an invention is obliged to manufacture the protected product or apply the protected process to satisfy national defense, security, healthcare/nutrition needs or other urgent social needs; failure may allow State authority to grant licenses. The owner of a mark shall be obliged to use it continuously; validity terminates if not used for a continuous period of more than 5 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use inventions can trigger compulsory licensing provisions (Article 136).

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations regarding dependent inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A dependent invention is created on the basis of another (principle) invention and can only be used on condition of using the principle invention. If the independent invention creates important technical advance or considerable economic significance, the owner of the dependent invention may request a license of the principle invention on reasonable commercial price and conditions; if the principle owner fails without justifiable reasons the State may grant a license to the dependent invention owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State competent authority may grant license under Articles 145 and 146 if requirements unmet (Article 137).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of industrial property rights (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment means transfer of ownership right by the industrial property owner to another organization or individual and shall be conducted in the form of a written contract (contract for assignment of industrial property right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory requirement: written contract (Article 138).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions to assignment of industrial property rights
rubrics_metrics.description: An owner shall only assign rights within the scope of protection. Rights to a geographical indication shall not be assigned. Rights to a trade name shall only be assigned together with transfer of the entire business premise and business activities under the trade name. Assignment of rights to a mark shall not cause confusion as to characteristics or origin of goods/services. Rights to a mark shall only be assigned to persons who fulfill registration requirements for that mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These restrictions limit alienability and protect consumers and prior rights (Article 139).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in contracts for assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: A contract for assignment of industrial property right shall have the following substantial provisions: 1. Full name and address of the assignor and the assignee; 2. Bases of assignment; 3. Price for assignment; 4. Rights and obligations of the assignor and the assignee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are mandatory substantive provisions for validity (Article 140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing of industrial property objects (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensing means permission by the industrial property owner to another organization or individual to use the industrial property object within the scope of the owner’s use right; licensing shall be conducted in the form of a written contract (license contract).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written license contract is required for licensing (Article 141).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions to licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to use a geographical indication or a trade name shall not be licensed. The right to use of a collective mark shall not be licensed to organizations or individuals other than members of the collective mark owner. The licensee shall not enter into a sub-license without permission of the licensor. A mark licensee must indicate on goods/packaging that the goods have been produced under a contract for use of mark. An invention licensee under an exclusive contract must use the invention in the same manner as the invention owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are per-object limitations and licensee obligations (Article 142).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: License contracts may be: 1. Exclusive license – licensee has exclusive right to use within scope and term and licensor cannot conclude other licenses or use the object without permission; 2. Non-exclusive license – licensor retains rights to use and grant other non-exclusive licenses; 3. Sub-license contract – where the licensor is a licensee under another contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines exclusivity and sub-licensing relationships (Article 143).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and prohibited terms in license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A license contract shall contain: a) Full name and address of licensor and licensee; b) Bases of the license; c) Type of the contract; d) Scope of the license (limitations; territorial); dd) Term; e) Price; g) Rights and obligations. The contract must not include provisions that unreasonably restrict the licensee, particularly: a) prohibiting licensee from improving the industrial property object (other than marks) or compelling licensee to grant free license or assign rights in improvements; b) directly/indirectly restricting licensee's export to territories where licensor does not hold rights; c) compelling licensee to buy materials/components from licensor without quality aim; d) prohibiting licensee from contesting validity of the industrial property right or the right to license. Such terms are invalid ex-officio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any terms listed as unreasonable are void automatically to protect licensee freedom and competition (Article 144).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bases for compulsory licensing of inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to use an invention shall be transferred to another by decision of a state competent authority without permission of the holder in cases: a) use for public non-commercial purposes (national defense, security, healthcare, nutrition, urgent social needs); b) holder fails to fulfill obligation to use invention upon expiration of 4 years from filing or 3 years from patent issue; c) user fails to reach agreement with holder after reasonable negotiation on adequate price/commercial considerations; d) holder determined to perform anti-competitive act under competition legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are statutory bases for compulsory licensing (Article 145).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to request termination of compulsory license
rubrics_metrics.description: The holder of exclusive right to use invention has the right to request termination of such right of use when the bases of compulsory licensing cease to exist and are unlikely to recur, provided termination is not prejudicial to the invention licensee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows restoration of exclusive rights when conditions that justified compulsory license end (Article 145.2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for compulsory license limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Transfers under compulsory decision must comply: a) right of use is non-exclusive; b) limited to scope and period sufficient to attain aim of compulsory licensing and predominantly for supply of domestic market (exceptions for anti-competition and semiconductor inventions); c) licensee shall not assign the right except with assignment of business premises nor grant sub-license; d) licensee shall pay adequate remuneration to holder taking into account economic value and government remuneration frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph 2 adds conditions for dependent inventions: holder of principal invention entitled to transfer right to use independent invention on reasonable terms; transferee shall not assign right except with assignment of whole right pertaining to independent invention (Article 146).

rubrics_metrics.name: Competency and procedures for compulsory licensing decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Minister of Science and Technology makes decisions on compulsory licensing for cases in Article 145 subparagraphs b, c and d. Ministries/ministerial-level authorities, based on consultation with the Minister, make decisions in their fields for cases under Article 145.1(d). Decision must provide appropriate scope/conditions per Article 146. State authority must promptly inform holder; decisions and refusals are subject to administrative appeal or judicial litigation. Government to make specific procedural provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies decision-makers, notification, appeal rights and that detailed procedures will be specified by Government (Article 147).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of contracts for transfer upon registration
rubrics_metrics.description: For industrial property rights established on registration basis, an assignment contract is effective only upon registration with the state administration authority. A contract for use is effective between parties as agreed but only effective to third parties upon registration. Validity of a licensing contract is terminated ex-officio upon termination of licensor's industrial property right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is crucial for third-party effect; licenses tied to underlying right (Article 148).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dossier contents for registration of transfer contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: A dossier for registration of a licensing contract or assignment shall comprise: a request for registration in prescribed form; an original or valid copy of the contract; the original of the Protection Title (for assignment); co-owners' written consent and explanation where co-ownership exists; receipt of fees/charges; power of attorney if filed through a representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These documents are required for processing registration (Article 149).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing dossiers for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The order and procedures of receiving and processing dossiers for registration of contracts for transfer of industrial property rights shall be provided by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural rules are delegated to Government regulations (Article 150).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial property representation service scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Industrial property representation service includes: a) representing organizations/individuals before state authorities competent in establishment and enforcement; b) advising on procedures for establishment and enforcement; c) other services concerning procedures for establishment and enforcement. Industrial property representatives include agencies and individual agents practicing for such organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines services and who qualifies as representative/agency (Article 151).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of rights and prohibitions for industrial property agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall only be entitled to provide services within scope of authorization and re-authorize another only with written consent. It may waive representation after legally transferring all pending works. An agency shall not: a) simultaneously represent parties in conflict of industrial property rights; b) withdraw an application, declare relinquishment, or withdraw an appeal without authorizing party consent; d) deceive or force clients to conclude/implement representation contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits conflicts of interest and unfair practices (Article 152).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities of industrial property representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: An industrial property representative shall: a) clearly notify items and rates of fees and charges and service charge tariff registered at the state authority; b) keep confidential all information and documents relating to a case; c) truthfully and completely inform the represented party about notifications/requirements of the state authority and deliver protection titles and decisions in time; d) protect legitimate rights and interests by satisfying requirements of the state authority in time; d') notify the state authority of changes in name, address and other information of the represented party where necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency has civil liabilities for activities performed by its agent (Article 153).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for conducting industrial property agency business
rubrics_metrics.description: An organization may conduct industrial property representation service if: 1) it is an enterprise, law firm, or scientific/technological service organization established and operating legally; 2) it has a function of conducting such business recorded in a certificate of business registration or operation registration; 3) the head or authorized person fulfills conditions for industrial property service practice under Article 155.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration and corporate form requirements must be satisfied (Article 154).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for practicing as an industrial property agent and certification
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual entitled to practice must: a) be granted a Practicing certificate of industrial property agent; b) work for one industrial property agency. To be granted the certificate one must: be a Vietnamese citizen with full civil capacity; reside permanently in Vietnam; have a university degree; have directly worked in industrial property legislation or examination for at least 5 consecutive years or have a recognized training certificate; not be an official/public servant of relevant state authorities; pass a profession exam organized by an authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government to make specific provisions for training program, examinations and granting certificates (Article 155).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordation, deletion and sanctions for industrial property representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations/individuals fulfilling conditions shall be recorded in the National Register and published. If they no longer fulfill conditions the state authority shall delete the name and publish. An agency violating provisions of Articles 152 and 153 shall be dealt with per laws; an agent making profession mistakes or violating certain provisions shall be subject to warning, monetary fine or revocation of practicing certificate depending on severity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registry and enforcement mechanisms exist including publication in the Official Gazette (Article 156).

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons eligible to hold rights for plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizations or individuals who bred or discovered and developed the plant variety or invested in the task to breed/discover/develop it or persons to whom rights were transferred; includes Vietnamese and foreign organizations/individuals that enter into agreements with Vietnam or foreigners with permanent residence or plant variety business/production establishment in Vietnam.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines eligible right-holders including transferees and investors (Article 157).

rubrics_metrics.name: General conditions for plant varieties to be protected
rubrics_metrics.description: A plant variety to be protected must be bred or discovered and developed, belong to the List of species able to be protected issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development, and be new, distinct, uniform, stable and have a proper denomination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All five substantive criteria (novelty, distinctness, uniformity, stability, proper denomination) plus inclusion in official list are required (Article 158).

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty of the plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety is deemed novel if propagating or harvested material has not been sold or distributed for exploitation by or with consent of right holder in Vietnam more than one year before application filing; or outside Vietnam more than six years before filing for trees or grape and four years for other species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different time-limits apply for within-Vietnam and foreign commercialization and for trees/grape vs other species (Article 159).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctness of the plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety is distinct if it is clearly distinguishable in one or more major characteristics from any other variety whose existence is common knowledge at the time of filing or priority date. Common knowledge varieties include those widely used in any country's market at filing, varieties protected or registered in any country, varieties subject of an application not refused, or varieties with published description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinctness is assessed against the set of varieties 'common knowledge' at filing (Article 160).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of the plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety is deemed uniform in propagation if there is the same expression of the relevant phenotype unless variation is permitted for certain characteristics in its propagation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniformity requirement pertains to propagation material and permitted exceptions for specified characteristics (Article 161).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of the plant variety
rubrics_metrics.description: The variety is stable if the relevant phenotypic characteristics retain the same expression as originally described and remain unchanged after each propagation crop or cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stability is assessed over propagation cycles to ensure consistent phenotype (Article 162).

rubrics_metrics.name: Denomination (naming) of plant variety and improper denominations
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrant must propose an appropriate name same as denomination registered in any country upon filing. A proper denomination is distinguishable from other varieties of common knowledge. Denominations are improper if: a) consist of numerals only (except when related to particularity); b) violate social morality; c) liable to misrepresent features/characteristics; d) easy to misunderstand about Breeder’s identification; d') identical or confusingly similar to a trade mark, trade name or geographical indication already protected before filing; e) identical or similar to the name of harvested products of such varieties; g) affecting prior rights of others. Anyone offering propagating material for sale must use the name as in the Protection Certificate even after expiry. When combined with a trademark, the name must be easily distinctive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects clarity, non-deceptiveness and prior rights; registrant must adhere to naming rules and reuse obligations (Article 163).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration of rights over plant varieties (who may file and state ownership)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain protection for a new plant variety, organizations and individuals must submit registration to the State administrative authority of industrial property rights. Registrants include breeders who directly bred/discovered/developed the variety by their efforts/expenses; organizations/individuals who invested for the breeder under contract unless otherwise agreed; organizations/individuals transferred or inherited the registration right. Varieties bred using State budget/managed project funds belong to the State; Government shall make specific provisions for registration in such cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies eligible applicants and government ownership of state-funded varieties (Article 164).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission and filing principles for plant variety applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Vietnamese organizations/individuals and qualifying foreigners may file applications directly or through legal representative in Vietnam. Foreigners without permanent address or establishment in Vietnam may file through a lawful representative. If more than one independent person files on different days, protection is granted to the earliest valid registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-to-file principle applies; representation rules for foreigners described (Articles 165-166).
